pairs.label: Data plane
pairs.detail: Clients, routers, cache nodes, replicas, and origin adapters serve GET, SET, and invalidation traffic.
pairs.explanation: Clients, routers, cache nodes, replicas, and origin adapters serve GET, SET, and invalidation traffic. They continue using the last valid ring during a short control plane outage.

pairs.explanation: Membership, health, placement, ring epochs, configuration, and repair orchestration change slowly and durably. They never coordinate every cache operation.

pairs.label: Derived read model
pairs.detail: Use cache-aside, asynchronous replicas, TTL jitter, and versioned invalidation.
pairs.explanation: Use cache-aside, asynchronous replicas, TTL jitter, and versioned invalidation. Brief staleness is acceptable because the durable record remains authoritative.

pairs.label: Session snapshot
pairs.detail: Route a user's reads to the acknowledged primary or carry a minimum version token until replicas catch up.
pairs.explanation: Route a user's reads to the acknowledged primary or carry a minimum version token until replicas catch up. Keep a durable recovery source if losing the session is unacceptable.

pairs.label: Coordination state
pairs.detail: Balances, locks, leases, and unique reservations need storage with explicit durability, consensus, and fencing semantics.
pairs.explanation: Balances, locks, leases, and unique reservations need storage with explicit durability, consensus, and fencing semantics. Fast in-memory access does not make weak ownership safe.

pairs.label: Smart client vs proxy router
pairs.detail: Smart clients remove a hop but distribute complex ring and retry logic.
pairs.explanation: Smart clients remove a hop but distribute complex ring and retry logic. Proxies centralize policy and isolate untrusted callers but add latency and their own capacity and availability requirements.

pairs.label: Consistent ring vs fixed slots
pairs.detail: A ring with virtual nodes supports weighted, incremental ownership.
pairs.explanation: A ring with virtual nodes supports weighted, incremental ownership. Fixed slots are easier to inspect and migrate explicitly but require a slot map and movement tooling.

pairs.label: Async vs sync replication
pairs.detail: Async copies preserve low write latency and availability with a staleness window.
pairs.explanation: Async copies preserve low write latency and availability with a staleness window. Sync acknowledgement narrows that window but waits for another failure domain and can reject writes during partitions.

pairs.label: RF=2 vs RF=3
pairs.detail: Two copies reduce memory and write amplification.
pairs.explanation: Two copies reduce memory and write amplification. Three copies improve placement, maintenance, and concurrent-failure options but increase footprint and repair work by 50%.

pairs.label: LRU vs LFU with aging
pairs.detail: LRU is simpler and fits temporal locality.
pairs.explanation: LRU is simpler and fits temporal locality. LFU with aging better protects stable hot sets from scans, at the cost of counters, sampling, and tuning.

pairs.label: Availability vs freshness
pairs.detail: Serving stale data can preserve reads during dependency failure.
pairs.explanation: Serving stale data can preserve reads during dependency failure. Strict namespaces must prefer version checks, primary reads, or temporary rejection when stale results violate the product contract.

pairs.label: Define namespace contracts
pairs.detail: Separate disposable derived data, session read-your-writes, and state that must remain in a durable coordination store.
pairs.explanation: Separate disposable derived data, session read-your-writes, and state that must remain in a durable coordination store.

pairs.label: Size the full envelope
pairs.detail: Couple hit rate, physical replicas, per-node benchmarks, zone-loss headroom, and origin fallback instead of sizing each metric independently.
pairs.explanation: Couple hit rate, physical replicas, per-node benchmarks, zone-loss headroom, and origin fallback instead of sizing each metric independently.

pairs.label: Route by a versioned ring
pairs.detail: Hash namespaced keys to virtual-node ranges, place replicas across failure domains, and cache membership metadata outside the request-time control plane.
pairs.explanation: Hash namespaced keys to virtual-node ranges, place replicas across failure domains, and cache membership metadata outside the request-time control plane.

pairs.label: Bound fills and updates
pairs.detail: Coalesce misses, limit origin work, add TTL jitter, and use source versions plus tombstones to stop stale fills and invalidations from racing.
pairs.explanation: Coalesce misses, limit origin work, add TTL jitter, and use source versions plus tombstones to stop stale fills and invalidations from racing.

pairs.label: Move and fail over gradually
pairs.detail: Promote replicas with fencing, transfer only affected ranges, protect foreground latency, and restore redundancy in the background.
pairs.explanation: Promote replicas with fencing, transfer only affected ranges, protect foreground latency, and restore redundancy in the background.

pairs.label: Operate the causal chain
pairs.detail: Correlate latency, hit rate, evictions, hot keys, origin load, replication lag, and ring changes; rehearse the failures that join those signals.
pairs.explanation: Correlate latency, hit rate, evictions, hot keys, origin load, replication lag, and ring changes; rehearse the failures that join those signals.
